leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer a single-part prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators. They share the view that band topology is a new organising principle, that the theory-then-experiment loop is closed, that roughly fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation make it mature, and that the 2016 prize did not cover time-reversal-invariant Z2 physics. They differ on citation wording: Danielsson and Johansson name the prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators with realisation in HgTe quantum wells, while Eriksson and Mehlig use broader wording on prediction and experimental discovery of the effect and of topological insulators. Danielsson and Eriksson want the citation confined to the 2D case. All four name the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and of the 3D pioneers as the weak point, and all four list B022 as an alternative. Eriksson and Mehlig also list B035 and B025 respectively; Johansson lists B023; Danielsson lists B028.

Four members prefer a single-part prize to Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks. They share the view that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 single-ion prize, that independent clocks at RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST and SYRTE agree near 10^-18, and that the two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist. All four name overlap with earlier prizes as the main reservation and all four list B039 as first alternative. Their citations differ in emphasis: Kroll centres on magic-wavelength trapping and the 10^-18 level, Lindroth adds new tests of fundamental physics, Olsson stresses invention and realisation, and Pearce stresses invention and development. Second alternatives differ (B025 for Kroll, B005 for Lindroth, B035 for Olsson, B049 for Pearce). Pearce moved to this position from B022 as a second choice after the opening round.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's round-1 configuration is a single-part prize built on either B039 or B022, and all eight members list the other of these two among their alternatives.
Both leading candidates are regarded as mature, with independent confirmation across several laboratories and no member arguing that either is premature.

Within the supplied names, no member proposes changing the trio Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the pair Katori, Ye; the disagreement is about whether the trio's credit is defensible and which candidate should be ranked first.

Any citation for B022 must name the magic-wavelength lattice concept explicitly so that it does not appear to reopen the 2005 and 2012 prizes (stated by Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, and acknowledged by supporters of B039).

Any B039 citation must be worded carefully about what the HgTe experiment tested, because the experiment followed the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal rather than the original Kane-Mele graphene proposal (Eriksson, Danielsson).

Two consecutive prizes in superconducting circuits (2025 and B023) are widely seen as hard to defend; Johansson, Eriksson, Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each state or imply reluctance, and Johansson has moved B023 to an alternative.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock counts as a discovery about nature or as a measurement refinement: Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig raise this against B022, while Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce answer that millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, constants and dark-matter tests, and many-body clock physics are new results; Lindroth herself notes it cuts against her taste for the unexpected.

Whether conceptual novelty (band topology as an organising principle, B039) should outweigh metrological impact and clean attribution (B022); Mehlig says B022 would win if precision were weighted above novelty.
Whether the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and the 3D topological insulators are one achievement or two (raised by Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson and Danielsson, unresolved).

Whether magic-angle graphene (B035) is mature enough: Olsson and Kroll cite device dependence, an unresolved pairing mechanism and an eight-year record, while Eriksson shares the maturity concern; no member prefers it as the leading part.

Whether the 10^-18 lattice-clock results are by themselves sufficient evidence, or whether single-ion clocks (Al+, Yb+) with competing accuracy and priority claims weaken the lattice-specific case (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce, Olsson).
attribution_disputes: B039: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the host that Molenkamp's group tested, and Zhang has died; Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy, Hasan and Cava established the 3D case. Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Danielsson and Olsson all flag this, and Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce cite it as their reason for not putting B039 first. Eriksson and Mehlig argue Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is the most coherent trio within the supplied names; Danielsson proposes handling Bernevig, Hughes and Hasan through external-expert requests.

B022: Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Hollberg and the ion-clock groups are outside the credited names (Lindroth, Olsson, Kroll, Pearce); Lindroth also asks whether Katori's early strontium demonstration and Ye's accuracy record are both needed. No member has independently verified the priority chronology.

B049: the BeppoSAX X-ray localisation (Costa, Frontera) is separate from the optical counterpart and redshift work (Kulkarni's group, van Paradijs, Djorgovski) and the afterglow theorists; Pearce lists it only as an alternative and Kroll and Mehlig express attribution doubts.

B028: Danielsson has moved it from his preferred configuration to an alternative because three leaders drawn from two collaborations of thousands do not reflect decisive individual contributions; Johansson and Pearce hold similar views, though Danielsson says the same objection applies nearly equally to B049.
B023: Girvin and Devoret are not among the credited names (Danielsson, Lindroth), leaving a gap in the credited trio.
maturity_disputes: Whether the redefinition of the SI second, still pending, should be awaited before B022: Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce say the result does not depend on it; Johansson and Mehlig are wary of the pending decision as a premature or external driver.

Whether the 2005 comb prize and 2012 single-ion prize leave room for a further precision-timekeeping prize: a committee judgement flagged by Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, and raised against B022 by Mehlig.

Whether the 2016 topological phase-transition prize narrows room for B039: Danielsson and Eriksson flag partial overlap, while Johansson and Mehlig see no real overlap with time-reversal-protected Z2 physics.
Whether B035 should wait: Olsson, Kroll and Danielsson accept the correlated phases as established but see the mechanism as open and the field as young.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs WACQT at Chalmers, co-authored the dynamical Casimir effect experiment, and knows the circuit-QED community; she names Delsing and Wilson as Chalmers colleagues and flags possible recusal on B023, which she has moved to an alternative.
Pearce is a member of the Fermi-LAT collaboration with field proximity to B049 and B003 and would consider recusing himself from B049 if it advances.

Kroll spent part of his PhD period in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Jun Ye is at JILA, which he calls a loose lineage and community link with no known collaboration with Katori or Ye; he also notes WACQT involvement relevant to B005, B025 and B023.
Lindroth has an attosecond and atomic-theory collaboration with Anne L'Huillier's Lund group (2023 laureate) and notes no collaboration with Katori or Ye.
Eriksson chaired the committee for the 2025 prize, which touches the same field as B023, and states no personal connection to its candidates.
Olsson notes long-running microscopy exchanges with Tokyo and Japanese groups with no tie to Katori or Ye, and that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague relevant only to B023.
Mehlig notes that Gothenburg and Chalmers physics are closely linked and that Johansson and Olsson are Gothenburg-based; no collaboration with a shortlisted candidate was found.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee write a B022 citation around the magic-wavelength lattice and the resulting 10^-18 accuracy that is clearly distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and which of Katori's early demonstration and Ye's accuracy record is essential to a two-name credit?

Can the committee defend a B039 citation limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with the HgTe realisation, to external reviewers given the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the death of Zhang, or would the 3D work require a different allocation?
Should the committee treat the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and 3D topological insulators as one achievement or two, and if as two, does any three-person set fit a single prize?

What new fact about nature has the optical lattice clock already delivered beyond a smaller error bar, as Danielsson asks, and does the committee weigh conceptual novelty above metrological impact when choosing between B039 and B022?
Should the pending redefinition of the SI second be treated as a consequence of the result or as a condition for awarding B022?
Would a two-part prize be considered, given that B039 and B022 together name five people and Johansson notes that any combined prize would have to fit a subset within three?

Which external expert reviews should the Secretary request before the final ballot on priority for B039 (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan, Fu, Moore, Balents), B022 (Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Hollberg) and B049 (BeppoSAX versus optical groups)?
Do members who flagged conflicts (Johansson on B023, Pearce on B049 and B003, Kroll and Lindroth on lineage links) need any formal recusal recorded for the shortlisted ballots that remain live?
summary.chair_observation: The committee is evenly split at four to four between B039 and B022, and every member lists the other candidate among their alternatives, so round 2 is mainly a choice between conceptual novelty with contested credit and metrological achievement with clean credit but overlap concerns with earlier prizes. I record that I moved B022 from second place to my preferred configuration after the openings, away from B049, and that astroparticle topics such as B049 and B003 are within my field while condensed-matter and quantum-information topics are outside it.
